narrative: Castlefield Traders looks healthy: a three-month revenue dip in January–March 2026 fully recovered by April, and margin, discount and tier mix all held steady or improved. The apparent declines in Diagnostic Equipment and Fasteners & Fittings are lumpy order patterns with occasional zero-order months, not sustained loss. No dimension shows a material, statistically meaningful shift.
cited_evidence: ,677, ₹108,360 and ₹88,239 in January–March 2026, revenue fully recovered to ₹213,956 by April 2026.
Margin rate held at 29.8% in the recent period versus 28.9% at baseline, no erosion.
Average discount edged down from 5.1% to 4.8%, showing no sign of discount creep.

model_agreement.agent_response: Agree: the model's healthy call is corroborated by the recovered dip and stable margin, discount and tier-mix figures.

evidence_timeline.headline: History begins
evidence_timeline.detail: 22.9 months of history, 30 orders across 8 categories. Data sufficiency: sufficient (score 1.0).

evidence_timeline.headline: Diagnostic Equipment revenue steps down 51.7%
evidence_timeline.detail: Monthly revenue Rs 38,595 -> Rs 18,628 (51.7%); 18.8% of this account's baseline revenue. Sustained 9 months. No prior-year echo, so seasonality does not explain it. This category has since recovered.
evidence_timeline.method: The stricter multi-year seasonal check needs about three years of history and could not run; the prior-year echo above is the check 24 months can support.

evidence_timeline.headline: Revenue dip, since recovered (2026-01 - 2026-03)
evidence_timeline.detail: 3 months below normal; trough Rs 88,239. Recovered from 2026-04. A resolved incident, not a live problem.

evidence_timeline.headline: The recent dip has no prior-year echo
evidence_timeline.detail: Dipped in 2026-01, 2026-02, 2026-03, but the same months a year earlier were normal. Seasonality does not explain this.

evidence_timeline.headline: Fasteners & Fittings revenue steps down 41.5%
evidence_timeline.detail: Monthly revenue Rs 28,985 -> Rs 16,947 (41.5%); 14.7% of this account's baseline revenue. Sustained 7 months. No prior-year echo, so seasonality does not explain it.
evidence_timeline.method: The stricter multi-year seasonal check needs about three years of history and could not run; the prior-year echo above is the check 24 months can support.

evidence_timeline.headline: Revenue drifting within its normal band
evidence_timeline.detail: First half vs second half -14.5%, trend -1.05%/month. This is drift, not a material decline.
evidence_timeline.method: Material decline requires both <= -15.0% half-over-half and <= -1.50%/month trend.

evidence_timeline.headline: Margin rate is stable
evidence_timeline.method: Erosion threshold: 3.0pp between the baseline and recent windows.

evidence_timeline.headline: Discounting is stable
evidence_timeline.method: Creep threshold: 3.0pp. Discount is revenue-weighted, so a deep discount on a large line counts for more than the same discount on a small one.

evidence_timeline.headline: Product mix is stable
evidence_timeline.detail: High-tier share of revenue 50.7% -> 54.1% (+3.4pp). Low tier 25.4% -> 24.1%.
evidence_timeline.method: Shift threshold: 8.0pp. Direction decides the verdict — the same size of move upward is premiumisation, not a downgrade.

evidence_timeline.headline: Ordering behaviour is unchanged
evidence_timeline.detail: Orders per month 1.28 -> 1.17 (-8.6%); lines per order 7.35 -> 6.29 (-14.4%); average order value 1.3%.

breakdown.note: Lines share the account's expected months of continued buying, so their values add back to the account total. Line losses can exceed the account's value at risk because lines that grew offset part of the loss.

_lifetime_value.note: Lifetime value = value per month x the horizon months (12 or 24), flat. Expected orders and expected active months (BG/NBD, fitted on the whole book) are reported alongside for information and do not scale the money. Baseline uses the value per month before the recent window; current uses the recent window. Value at risk is the gap — the same loss the monthly figures show, on a longer clock. Never add it to monthly revenue at risk.
